brand.title: IQVIA (Production)
brand.subtitle: Knowledge Check — Introduction to CTFS for TechIQ

questions.question: What does CTFS stand for?
questions.feedback_correct: That's right—CTFS is IQVIA's Clinical Trial Financial Suite, designed to unify financial operations across clinical trials.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Not quite. While these sound similar, CTFS specifically stands for Clinical Trial Financial Suite. This foundational term appears in the course introduction.

questions.question: According to the course, by what percentage did trial sites grow since 2019?
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—the course notes that trial sites grew by 49 percent since 2019, contributing to the increased complexity in clinical trial management.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course states that trial sites grew by 49 percent since 2019. You may have confused this with the 60 percent increase in protocol amendments mentioned on the same slide.

questions.question: What is one key problem that fragmented financial processes create for clinical trials?
choices: Manual data entry that creates errors and requires re-entry across multiple systems
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—fragmentation causes staff to re-enter the same information into multiple systems, which increases errors and limits visibility.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While trial complexity has many impacts, the course specifically highlights that fragmented processes cause manual data entry errors and information duplication across disconnected systems.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a capability included in CTFS?
questions.feedback_correct: Right—patient recruitment and enrollment marketing are not part of CTFS. The platform focuses on financial workflows, not recruitment activities.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course lists six financial capabilities within CTFS: budgeting, contracting, forecasting, site payments, participant payments, and exception management. Recruitment marketing falls outside the financial scope of the platform.

questions.question: How does CTFS shift the nature of financial work in clinical trials?
choices: From site involvement to sponsor-only control
From manual workflows to orchestrated, AI-enabled processes that focus human attention on exceptions
From global operations to domestic-only operations
From data verification to data elimination
questions.feedback_correct: Precisely—CTFS moves from repetitive manual tasks to orchestrated workflows where AI handles routine work and humans focus on decisions requiring expertise.
questions.feedback_incorrect: CTFS is designed to automate routine financial tasks while keeping humans in control of critical decisions. The goal is smarter orchestration, not removing oversight or changing the relationship between sites and sponsors.

questions.question: What does 'agentic AI' mean in the context of CTFS?
choices: AI that replaces all human decision-making in financial processes
AI that works independently without any connection to other systems
AI capabilities that perform or support connected tasks within a broader workflow, orchestrated through the platform
AI that is only used for participant communication
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—agentic AI in CTFS refers to AI agents that work together through orchestration via APIs and webhooks, not as isolated tools.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Agentic AI in CTFS is not about replacing humans or working in isolation. Instead, it's about multiple AI agents that are coordinated through the platform to support connected workflows like document ingestion, forecasting, and reconciliation.

questions.question: According to the course, what is the projected reduction in financial processing time that CTFS can deliver?
questions.feedback_correct: That's correct—the course cites a projected 50 percent reduction in financial processing time as a key outcome of CTFS implementation.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While CTFS offers significant efficiency gains, the course specifically states a projected 50 percent faster financial processing as a proven outcome.

questions.question: How many countries does CTFS support for participant payments?
questions.feedback_correct: Well done—CTFS supports participant payments across more than 180 countries, reflecting IQVIA's global infrastructure.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course states that CTFS's participant payment capabilities extend across more than 180 countries, as part of its global-by-design approach to supporting international trials.

questions.question: What is the recommended starting approach for implementing CTFS according to the course?
choices: Implement all CTFS modules simultaneously across the entire organization
Wait until all roadmap features are complete before beginning any implementation
Launch a focused pilot tied to a measurable business problem, integrate specific capabilities, and establish baseline metrics
Replace all existing financial systems immediately to avoid confusion
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—the course recommends starting with a focused pilot that addresses a specific business problem, measures outcomes, and creates a scaling path.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course emphasizes a phased approach rather than a big-bang transformation. A focused pilot tied to measurable metrics helps establish value and reduces implementation risk before broader scaling.

questions.question: Which of the following best synthesizes why the timing is right for CTFS adoption according to the course?
choices: IQVIA needs to increase revenue from software sales
Growing trial complexity, increased site numbers, and protocol amendments make fragmented financial processes increasingly costly and difficult to manage effectively
Regulatory agencies are requiring all sponsors to use cloud-based systems
Participants are demanding more transparency in sponsor payments
questions.feedback_correct: Precisely—you've identified the core strategic case: complexity is outpacing current capabilities, making the need for unified, automated financial management both urgent and compelling.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While several factors support CTFS adoption, the course emphasizes that growing trial complexity (49% more sites, 60% more amendments) combined with fragmented processes creates both operational delays and measurable costs that CTFS addresses directly.
